newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Van der Horst plunges to 45-month low.
newsitem.headline: Van der Horst plunges to 45-month low.

text.p: Shares of Indonesian-linked Van der Horst plunged to a 45-month low of Singapore $1.98 in early Tuesday trade after the infrastructure company reported an 84 percent profit dive for the six months ended March 31, 1997.
At 0125 GMT, the shares were trading around Singapore $2.07, down 12 cents, on over 2.7 million shares traded. The shares last went below $2.00 in October 1993 when they traded at S$1.93.
On Monday, the engineering-based company reported net profit dived to S$4.14 million, and turnover eroded about 63 percent to S$27.56 million.
Van der Horst also said onMonday that banks had to sell a portion of shares pledged as collateral by its major shareholders -- Johannes Kotjo, Johnlin Yuwono and Bambang Trihatmodjo.
According to the Edinburgh Financial Publishing's Estimate directory, Van der Horst's net earnings for the full year ending September 30, 1997 were forecast at S$65 million.
The poor performance was blamed on delays in three projects in Indonesia -- Jakarta Depot Satellite and Surabaya Depot Satellite pipelines and the Semarang power plant.
